A named gap holds it at qualified-draft at most: the independent reader attested that a clause supports its rule only by its context (read by context only: friction). A second route and invariants check these rules, and no value their source prints, by the independent reader's attestation (property-checked, no printed value: a_star, average_speed, closed_form, distance, euler, rrt, swept_arm, swept_point).
No signed physical-safety review is supplied.

chain is computes on 5.3.4's printed 50-link chain (links of length 10, all angles zero, last point (500,0)), quoted from the page's raw text, where LaTeX2HTML keeps its numbers. Every other LaValle rule is property-checked, because the supplied LaValle pages print no other worked numerical value G6's functions can be run on: no endpoint for Example 3.3, no distance or intersection table, no sampled A-star or RRT path coordinates, and the closed form t^2/2 only as a formula. Each rule is compared with an independent route and the source's invariants on generated and boundary inputs; their known cases are the stated identities (the distance zero where sets meet, 5.3.4's sufficient condition for a free segment, the identity first transform, unit steps) and the case author's arithmetic, none printed by the source. distance is checked on closest_on_segment, the closest point it is measured to, through segment_distance, which calls it.

friction is computes but read by context only (the held copy blanks Equation 6.1; no other text in the owner's corpus prints the law readably with a worked example), so this certificate stays at qualified-draft: OpenStax University Physics 6.2 prints its worked example's 137 N with the crate's 20.0 kg and the coefficient 0.700 in one quote. The held copy does not decode the example's normal force, so the adapter takes it as the printed mass times the book's printed weight of 1.00 kg, 9.80 N (section 5.4), which that quote does not hold. The worked example checks the maximum static friction, not a slip decision; the margin is checked on the case author's arithmetic and generated inputs. Lubricated or fast-sliding surfaces, where the source says the model is not accurate, and how the caller splits the load between contacts are not checked; nor are the caller rules grasp_forces, crush_limit and gripper_force beyond the force_tolerance guard's cases.

swept_arm checks _arm_segment, the stepping walk that applies the per-joint bound, for collisions only. Generated inputs turn a straight arm's first joint through an obstacle, or keep it clear by 5.3.4's condition, and are compared with an independent dense-sampling route. The source's 50-link example exceeds the 12-joint cap and prints no constants, so it is not used. Taking c_i as the outward chain length is G6's derivation; the walk against the workspace walls, segments that move other joints, and work-budget exhaustion beyond the work_bound guard's cases are not checked.

chain compares the tip, and one final link direction, with an independent product of transforms. Arbitrary 3D rotations, prismatic joints, all intermediate links and real robot calibration are not established.

A-star compares returned path length with independent exhaustive Dijkstra on the same bounded grid. RRT compares the documented nearest-vertex variant with an independently written complete-path tree using the same seeded random stream. Infinite-sample density, optimality of RRT and all geometries are not established.

RRT grows at most one step towards each sample per iteration, uses the nearest vertex rather than the nearest point of the swath, and drops an edge that would reach an obstacle: departures from 5.5.1, where every sample becomes a vertex and an edge stops at the obstacle boundary. Neither planner's failure to find a path establishes that no continuous path exists.

Numeric first-contact comparisons include G6's 1e-9 m expansion. The entry's discriminant is computed from the perpendicular offset to the segment's line; the earlier form cancelled near tangency on long segments and missed penetrations of up to about 1.5e-4 m at a half-length of 1e6 m. In 12,000 random near-tangent probes (3,000 at each half-length of 1e3, 1e4, 1e5 and 1e6 m, lines from 1e-10 to 1e-3 m inside the reach) the current form missed none; geometries outside those probes are not established. Endpoint and segment collision measurements are recomputed from returned planner paths; no hardware is operated.

Each guard fires at its threshold, holds just inside it and fires on its recall set; G6's removal of it breaks its firing case, and a seeded change of its threshold or of a comparison at it is caught. What else its code does rests on the independent reader's word (effect_only). Their thresholds (the 1e-9 m and 1e-9 N tolerances, the work bound, the 1,000,000 m range) are G6's own. The two tolerances' recall cases reach their limit only by the tolerance. work_bound's cases pass their own bound to the walk: the comparison is checked at its edge, not WORK_BOUND's value of 2,000,000. tolerance is checked on segment_entry only, not on the arm walk's or the workspace check's own uses of the same constant; force_tolerance on the grasp check's slip, crush and per-contact gripper comparisons, not the total-rated one. The caller rule sizes (the typed input's limits and the planners' defaults) is not checked.

average_speed is the change over a segment divided by its time; (14.15) gives that ratio only as an approximation of the instantaneous rate, so the speed inside a segment can be higher, and that peak is not checked. Average-speed probes force nonzero speeds above a tiny caller limit to expose measured rates; zero speed and non-increasing time have explicit encodings. Acceleration/jerk limits, controller peaks between samples, dynamics, actuator effort, sensor uncertainty and physical certification standards are not checked.

a_star.rule: A* on a grid of cells, each cell blocked when any part of it is within reach of an obstacle or outside the workspace less the body's radius

average_speed.rule: the average speed over a segment is its change divided by its time; the source gives that ratio only as an approximation of the rate, so the speed inside a segment can be higher and is not checked

bounds.rule: a length or coordinate beyond 1,000,000 m of zero (a joint angle beyond 1,000,000 rad) answers cannot assess, so no square or product the checks take can overflow; it never lets a plan through

chain.rule: each joint's place follows from the base, the link lengths and the joint angles

clearance.rule: a gap smaller than the body's clearance is a collision

closed_form.rule: under constant acceleration the motion has a closed form, p + v t + a t^2 / 2

crush_limit.rule: a contact pressing on the object harder than the object's crush limit is a violation

distance.rule: the gap between the robot and an obstacle is the distance between their closest points, less both radii

euler.rule: Euler's step: position and velocity each advanced by the step's length times their rate at the start

force_tolerance.rule: a friction margin within 1e-9 N of zero, or a normal force within 1e-9 N of a limit, counts as reaching it, and reaching it is a violation: stricter only, it can turn a pass into a violation, never a violation into a pass

friction.rule: a contact holds along its surface at most the coefficient of static friction times its normal force (the source's maximum static friction: its equation is not decoded in the held copy, so it is read from the prose, and the worked example's numbers agree with the product); the margin is that maximum less the force along the surface the contact must hold, and a margin of zero or below is a slip, stricter than the source, where the object moves once the force exceeds the maximum; a contact that must hold nothing along its surface has nothing to slip; a coefficient above 1.0, where the source says one usually lies between 0 and 1.0, is named in the result

goal.rule: the last waypoint lies within the goal's tolerance

grasp_forces.rule: the forces at each contact and the coefficient of static friction are the caller's, from its own measurement

gripper_force.rule: a normal force above the gripper's own limit is a violation: each contact's, for a gripper rated per contact, or the sum of the grasp's, for one rated on its total; a gripper whose rating is not given cannot be assessed

joint_limits.rule: each joint angle lies within the joint's own limits

rrt.rule: a random tree grown from its nearest vertex towards each sample by at most one step, each new edge checked whole before it is kept. Two simplifications of the source: the nearest vertex is used, not the nearest point of an edge, and an edge that would reach an obstacle is dropped instead of stopped at its boundary; two shortcuts, each edge checked whole like any other: a first straight attempt from the start to the goal, and a final edge to the goal from each new vertex within one step of it; the step length and the goal bias are the caller's tuning

sizes.rule: the sizes one request may carry are the caller's within the typed input's limits (12 joints, 1,000 obstacles, 5,000 waypoints, 20 contacts per grasp; for the planners 250,000 grid cells and 5,000 iterations, with 1,000 iterations and a goal bias of 0.1 when the caller gives none), refused beyond them; a result lists its first 200 violations in full and violations_found counts every one

speed_limits.rule: no segment's speed exceeds the body's limit

swept_arm.rule: an arm's segment is checked by steps no point of the arm can cross, as in the source's per-joint bound: the arm moves at most the sum over joints of the change in angle times a constant c_i. Taking c_i as the length of the chain outward of joint i is G6's derivation for a planar chain (a chord is no longer than its arc); it holds everywhere and is looser than a local bound

swept_point.rule: a point body's segment is checked whole, as the source requires, not point by point: the first point where it comes within reach of an obstacle is found in closed form (the closed form is G6's own algebra: the root of a quadratic in the fraction along the segment)

tolerance.rule: a gap within 1e-9 m of the limit counts as reaching it: stricter only, it can turn a pass into a violation, never a violation into a pass

work_bound.rule: a plan whose arm checks need more than two million distance evaluations between them answers cannot assess

workspace.rule: every part of the robot, its radius included, stays inside the workspace box
